en.heading: 30 November: the Philippines honours revolutionary Andrés Bonifacio by law
en.origin: Philippine Act No. 2946, approved on 16 February 1921, amended the Administrative Code to make 30 November of each year a legal holiday. The National Museum of the Philippines identifies the date as the birth anniversary of Andrés Bonifacio, born on 30 November 1863, a key figure in the struggle against Spanish colonial rule. The act's original text and Senate legislative register establish the legal founding milestone; the museum provides the historical connection to Bonifacio's role in the Katipunan revolutionary organization. The designation is not the date of the Philippine Revolution itself, and the law does not independently document the first annual public ceremony after approval. Accordingly the first observed year is left unknown rather than assumed to be 1921.
en.promoter: The Fifth Philippine Legislature enacted Act No. 2946 in February 1921; Bonifacio is the historical figure commemorated, not the statute's personal drafter.
en.purpose: Remember revolutionary contributions to Philippine independence and encourage historical and civic education.
facts: Act No. 2946 was approved on 16 February 1921.

Il testo originale della legge e il registro del Senato provano il passaggio giuridico; il Museo documenta il legame storico con la società rivoluzionaria Katipunan. Il giorno scelto non coincide con l'avvio della rivoluzione filippina e la legge non dimostra autonomamente la prima cerimonia annuale dopo l'adozione. L'anno della prima celebrazione ufficiale rimane quindi sconosciuto, senza dedurlo dal 1921.

en.heading: 9 April: the Philippines remembers Bataan with a statutory Day of Valor
en.origin: The Philippines' Republic Act No. 3022, approved on 6 April 1961, proclaimed 9 April Bataan Day and established it as a legal holiday in memory of the soldiers and civilians who defended the Bataan Peninsula during the Second World War. The date recalls the surrender of forces on Bataan on 9 April 1942, preceding the brutal Bataan Death March. Article 1 of the 1961 statute explicitly asks people to observe one minute of silence at 4:30 in the afternoon. In 1987 President Corazon Aquino's Executive Order 203 listed the date among regular holidays under the name Araw ng Kagitingan, or Day of Valor, commemorating Bataan and Corregidor. The 1961 founding law, 1942 military event and 1987 name are distinct; the source does not independently prove the first official public ceremony after adoption.

en.heading: 12 June: the Philippine declaration of independence
en.origin: On 12 June 1898, Filipino revolutionaries proclaimed independence at Emilio Aguinaldo's home in Kawit, Cavite. The date recalls an assertion of national self-determination, not the year when the modern holiday law was enacted. President Diosdado Macapagal had already declared 12 June 1962 a special nationwide public holiday to observe Philippine Independence Day through Proclamation No. 28; this earlier annual-date observance must not be mistaken for the later statutory change. President Diosdado Macapagal declared 12 June 1964 a special public holiday through Proclamation No. 252. Republic Act No. 4166, approved on 4 August 1964, then changed the legal date of Independence Day from 4 July to 12 June and designated 4 July as Philippine Republic Day. These historical, commemorative and legislative milestones are distinct.

fr.origin: Le 12 juin 1898, des révolutionnaires philippins ont proclamé l'indépendance au domicile d'Emilio Aguinaldo, à Kawit dans la province de Cavite. Dès 1962, par la proclamation nº 28, le président Diosdado Macapagal avait déclaré le 12 juin jour férié spécial dans tout le pays pour commémorer l'indépendance, avant la modification légale ultérieure. Par la proclamation nº 252, le président Diosdado Macapagal a fait du 12 juin 1964 un jour férié spécial. La loi de la République nº 4166, approuvée le 4 août 1964, a ensuite déplacé officiellement la fête de l'indépendance du 4 juillet au 12 juin et renommé le 4 juillet Journée de la République philippine. Déclaration, proclamation présidentielle et loi sont trois jalons différents.
fr.promoter: Les révolutionnaires menés par Emilio Aguinaldo ; puis Diosdado Macapagal et le Congrès ont fixé la commémoration moderne.

Das am 4. August 1964 verabschiedete Republikgesetz Nr. 4166 verlegte den offiziellen Unabhängigkeitstag vom 4. Juli auf den 12. Juni und bestimmte den 4. Juli zum Tag der philippinischen Republik. Erklärung von 1898, Proklamation und Gesetz von 1964 sind getrennte Etappen.

pt.heading: 12 de junho: a declaração de independência das Filipinas
pt.origin: Em 12 de junho de 1898, revolucionários filipinos proclamaram a independência na casa de Emilio Aguinaldo, em Kawit, Cavite. A data recorda o acontecimento histórico, não o ano da lei que definiu a comemoração moderna. Já em 1962, pela Proclamação n.º 28, o presidente Diosdado Macapagal tinha declarado 12 de junho feriado especial em todo o país para comemorar a independência, antes da alteração legal posterior. Pela Proclamação n.º 252, o presidente Diosdado Macapagal declarou 12 de junho de 1964 feriado especial. A Lei da República n.º 4166, aprovada em 4 de agosto de 1964, transferiu depois a data legal do Dia da Independência de 4 de julho para 12 de junho e designou 4 de julho como Dia da República Filipina. A declaração, a proclamação e a lei são marcos diferentes.

en.heading: National Heroes Day: remembering many lives, not one name
en.origin: The Philippine National Heroes Day honours people who contributed to the country's struggle for independence and to its civic history, rather than one named historical figure. Act No. 3827 established an official National Heroes Day in 1931 on the last Sunday of August. Later holiday legislation, including Republic Act No. 9492, placed the observance on the last Monday of August; the 2026 government calendar lists 31 August. The original law, later scheduling and the history being remembered are separate facts.
en.promoter: The Philippine Legislature established the official observance through Act No. 3827; subsequent legislation adjusted the recurring holiday rule.
en.purpose: Commemorate collective service and sacrifice in Philippine history without reducing national heroism to a single individual.

it.heading: Giornata degli eroi nazionali: una memoria collettiva

Il calendario nazionale del 2026 indica il 31 agosto. La legge originaria e le successive regole del calendario sono momenti diversi.

en.heading: 30 December: Rizal Day and the memory of reform
en.origin: Rizal Day is the Philippine national remembrance of José Rizal and his execution on 30 December. Act No. 345 of 1 February 1902 subsequently included 30 December among public holidays. Later laws and annual proclamations maintain its status as a regular holiday; the 2026 calendar also lists it. Republic Act No. 11014, approved 5 April 2018, subsequently made 23 January a nationwide special working holiday and assigned educational activities to the Historical Commission and Education Department. en.heading: 12 August: the National Library's roots begin with a royal order in 1887
en.origin: The National Library of the Philippines preserves printed and recorded materials, books and documentary heritage that support public research, reading and the transmission of Filipino cultural memory. Royal Order No. 689 of 12 August 1887 established the Museo-Biblioteca de Filipinas in Manila, which the National Library identifies as its earliest institutional origin. This is the date used for the current founding anniversary. A separate American Circulating Library opened publicly on 9 March 1900; Public Act No. 96 of 5 March 1901 then reorganized and transferred library functions. Later names included Philippine Library and National Library, so the 1887 date and the 1900 public-library movement remain distinct.

en.heading: 19 September: the Order of Gabriela Silang in the Philippine Honors Code
en.origin: The Order of Gabriela Silang is one of the official honors listed by the Philippine state. It carries the name of Gabriela Silang, a figure of resistance against Spanish colonial rule in the eighteenth century. Executive Order No. 236, dated 19 September 2003, established the Honors Code and placed the Order of Gabriela Silang in the third tier of civilian honors, separating its protocol status from other named orders. The Code says that the order may be awarded to spouses of Filipino or foreign heads of state or government. Its purpose differs from the Order of Lakandula, which recognizes political and civic merit, even though both appear in the same 2003 code.

en.heading: May: National Heritage Month across the Philippines
en.origin: Philippine National Heritage Month takes place every May. President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo declared it through Proclamation No. 439 on 11 August 2003, drawing on constitutional commitments to conserve cultural heritage and recognizing both tangible places and living traditions. The proclamation asked government agencies to undertake heritage activities and appointed the National Commission for Culture and the Arts as lead agency. May was chosen partly because community festivals and local celebrations have long taken place during that month. This is an awareness month, not a month-long public holiday.

Il provvedimento invitò le amministrazioni a organizzare attività culturali e affidò il coordinamento alla National Commission for Culture and the Arts. en.heading: December: Rizal Month in the Philippines
en.origin: Rizal Month is a Philippine national cultural observance running throughout December. President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo proclaimed it on 26 November 2001 through Proclamation No. 126. The measure explained that commemorations limited to the period near Rizal Day had not provided enough time for educational, historical and civic activities honouring José Rizal. It asked government bodies, education institutions and community organizations to support events across the whole month. Rizal Month is a commemorative program and must not be confused with the separate regular public holiday of Rizal Day on 30 December.
